column3:
Your AI agent is only as safe as the network path you forgot to close.

Recent real-world incidents highlight an uncomfortable truth: calling something a sandbox does not make it a security boundary.

For platform teams, safer autonomy starts with four practical controls:

- Block outbound access by default; allow only named destinations.

- Issue short-lived credentials with the minimum required access.

- Run tools in isolated environments with explicit policy checks.

- Monitor every action and stop runs when behavior crosses a boundary.

The takeaway: treat AI agents like production workloads, not trusted shortcuts.

If an agent can reach it, change it, or send data to it, that path belongs in your threat model.

Which guardrail would your team put in place first?
